operations.title: Fundamental-cycle incidence pairing across inequivalent flavor smoothing normals
operations.body: For each common canonical boundary tree, embed each smoothing normal as its signed fundamental cycle and test nonzero labelled edge-incidence contraction, allowing exact tree automorphisms.

operations.title: A source-derived fundamental-cycle kernel connects the flavor coefficient occurrence module
operations.body: Identity gluing of smoothing normals has 14 components, but the signed occurrence pairing of their fundamental cycles is nonzero on 370 carrier component pairs and contains a 33-edge spanning tree across all 34 components. Thus the coefficient occurrence module is connected by a nontrivial incidence kernel. Weak-basis-invariant physical descent is not yet established.

operations.title: Nima reports that the fundamental-cycle kernel reconnects flavor coefficient occurrences
operations.body: The allowed incidence bridge closes the 14-way identity-gluing obstruction. For each tree T and normal e, form the signed fundamental cycle c_e in T+e; the labelled edge contraction <c_e,c_f> is nonzero on 370 component pairs and contains a 33-edge spanning tree across all 34 components. Thus the coefficient occurrence module is connected by a nontrivial source-derived kernel. The remaining falsifier is whether this contraction descends to weak-basis-invariant physical data.

operations.title: Flavor now realizes carrier-to-coefficient comparison by a nontrivial incidence kernel
operations.body: Follow-up to the 14-component normal-line obstruction: the predeclared fundamental-cycle incidence pairing reconnects the full coefficient occurrence module. It is nonzero on 370 component pairs and has a 33-edge spanning tree. Flavor therefore realizes Entry 1213's arrow sharply: exact connected carrier; identity coefficient gluing fails; a source-derived incidence kernel restores coefficient connectivity; physical weak-basis descent remains open.
